title: Canadian, Italian and Swiss cyber agencies warn autonomous AI agents are accelerating cyberattacks
date_note: CybersecAsia's article of 27 November summarises the agencies' warnings, which it dates 21 to 24 November; the Canadian page shows only a modified date of 2026-10-26.
org: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security; Italy's ACN; Switzerland's NCSC
geo_basis: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, agency
summary: CybersecAsia reports that Canada's Cyber Centre, Italy's national cybersecurity agency and Switzerland's NCSC have warned about attackers using autonomous AI agents. The Cyber Centre's bulletin says the agentic framework ARTEX was used against hundreds of organizations and that attacks are not yet fully autonomous, since humans still choose targets. CybersecAsia reports that Switzerland's NCSC reported its first confirmed AI-agent-assisted attacks on 24 November.
plain: Cyber agencies in Canada, Italy and Switzerland warn that attackers are using AI agents to speed up attacks. Canada says humans still choose targets and set objectives.
exec: Agencies say AI-agent tooling speeds attacks, so patching and response windows shrink.
action: The Canadian Cyber Centre advises requiring phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication for administrators and remote access, and patching Internet-facing systems promptly.

validation.note: The Canadian bulletin (page shows only 'date modified 2026-10-26') was read directly; the Italian and Swiss alerts are known only through CybersecAsia and were not read.
